title: Implement weather cards, freshness cache and local pressure context
verify: Record honest pre-implementation RED for every owned FT-002 AC and integration claim before changing production behavior; preserve any already-green condition rather than changing it without need.

Run deterministic redacted fixtures for current/daily normalization, selected-city timezone/day-night selection, moon and unknown-condition fallback, ordered four-card projection, sign rule, all 78 palette entries, endpoint clamp and shared static pseudo-glass.

Run isolated freshness/cache/history probes for launch, valid city change, 30-minute refresh, successful-cache-only persistence, 24-hour offline availability, stale four-contour rendering, installation-relative seven-day retention, first-run Yesterday and pressure thresholds/fallback.

Inspect Weather Context ownership and every crossed edge against Boundary Map, Capability Interfaces, Platform Runtime, Weather Provider, Local Data and Local Secret Handling; no direct Main Display/provider-adapter/private-storage bypass is permitted.

Verify launch, valid city-change and 30-minute network refresh use the accepted Android Runtime signal/wiring path: Android OS owns the signals, the Application Composition Root and Android Runtime Adapter only lift them, and Weather Context owns refresh/freshness/failure behavior; no new graph edge is permitted.

Verify the clock, timer lifecycle, cancellation and overdue dismissal remain usable during network/provider failure without adopting FT-001, FT-003, FT-004, FT-005, FT-006, FT-007, FT-008 or FT-009 behavior.

Use synthetic credentials only and record only redacted results. Host build/unit/static/fixture checks are mandatory. Apply the target-device route for card readability/static pseudo-glass only as deferred, non-blocking follow-up when host checks cannot establish the result; record DEFERRED plus residual risk when unavailable and never claim runtime PASS without a target.

GREEN: exactly yesterday/today/tomorrow/day-after is observed, Today is slightly larger and the other three sizes are equal smaller. Compare each order/size condition; artifact is the deterministic projection/layout assertion.

[FT-002-AC-002; REQ-005; REQ-022] Expected RED: no accepted normalized current/daily card mapping is present. GREEN: filled cards contain date, temperature, illustration and temperature background without textual day/weather labels, with selected-city timezone driving weather date/day-night and moon fallback; device clock/date remains FT-001-owned. Compare fixture fields to the canonical projection; artifact is redacted mapping/projection output.

[FT-002-AC-003; REQ-006; REQ-023] Expected RED: the Foundation surface has no accepted palette/material projection. GREEN: the −4…+4 sign rule, all 78 explicit colors, endpoint clamp and shared static pseudo-glass pass; host/static readability conditions pass, while target readability/static-visual evidence is deferred/non-blocking where host checks are insufficient. Compare every palette/material condition; artifact is mandatory host evidence plus DEFERRED target evidence and residual risk when unavailable.

[FT-002-AC-004; REQ-007; REQ-025] Expected RED: no feature-level refresh/freshness state is present. GREEN: launch, valid city change and 30-minute network refresh retain the last successful normalized result; cache age through 24 hours remains offline, older data renders four value-free contours, and clock/timer paths remain usable on failure. Compare each trigger/state/failure condition; artifact is deterministic cache/lifecycle and redacted integration output.

[FT-002-AC-005; REQ-008] Expected RED: the Foundation surface has no installation-relative pressure history or trend projection. GREEN: seven-day retention, 3-hour thresholds, exact-zero 12-hour fallback, Yesterday maximum-change rule, absent-arrow behavior and dated first-run contour pass without layout shift. Compare each history/trend condition; artifact is isolated host probe output.

[FT-002-AC-006; REQ-026] Expected RED: unknown condition or missing optional field is not handled by the feature surface. GREEN: neutral cloud/regular-moon fallbacks preserve available temperature/color, do not invent text and do not crash. Compare the redacted missing-field fixture result; artifact is the deterministic fallback test output.

[FT-002-AC-007; REQ-024] FT-002-AC-007 RED_NOT_APPLICABLE: meaningful pre-implementation RED cannot be produced without introducing a real or user-like credential into source, packaged resources, logs, fixtures, screenshots or evidence, which REQ-024 and the local-secret boundary forbid; alternative proof: provider and test paths use a synthetic credential only, the real key is absent from source, packaged resources, logs, fixtures, screenshots and evidence, and the isolated redacted scan compares that absence condition; artifact is the secret/artifact scan receipt; FT-008 remains the owner of user-facing key input/validation.
purpose: Turn the Foundation weather seam into the accepted FT-002 Weather Context outcome while preserving the approved Main Display boundary, local ownership, freshness/history lifecycle and redacted provider path.
success_outcome: A clean build and redacted deterministic evidence prove the four ordered weather cards, accepted presentation, provider normalization, 24-hour cache/freshness, seven-day local pressure context and failure fallbacks through the registered capability boundaries, without secret leakage or scope expansion.
anti_goals: Do not replace or re-plan FT-001 clock/date/fullscreen/colon/city-gesture behavior; consume its approved display shell seam.
Do not implement hourly or long-term forecast sessions from FT-003 or FT-004.
Do not implement preset configuration, countdown, cancellation, overdue state or alert behavior from FT-005, FT-006 or FT-007.
Do not implement Settings catalog, API-key input/validation, or personalization controls from FT-008 or FT-009; use only the accepted validated input boundary.
Do not add a backend, cloud sync, accounts, Google Services, reboot recovery, second provider, event infrastructure, realtime blur, new dependency or new graph edge.
Do not use live credentials or fabricate target-device/runtime evidence.

forbidden_scope: FT-001 clock/date/fullscreen/colon/city-gesture behavior beyond the approved weather projection seam
FT-003 and FT-004 forecast-session UI/state and forecast-specific completeness behavior
FT-005, FT-006 and FT-007 timer/preset/countdown/overdue/alert behavior
FT-008 Settings catalog/API-key input/validation and FT-009 personalization controls
direct reads or writes of Main Display, Settings & Location, Timer & Alert or Forecast Sessions private storage
direct Main Display access to provider adapters or raw provider fields
real API keys or secret-bearing source, logs, screenshots, fixtures or evidence
backend, cloud sync, accounts, Google Services, reboot recovery, event/message infrastructure or new permissions
stop_conditions: Stop and route to /spec-design if the implementation requires a new module, graph edge, public contract, ownership rule, UI toolkit/dependency or composition-root business orchestration.
Stop and route to /feature-doctor FT-002 or /write-prd if the accepted card order, freshness window, forecast horizon, timezone split, fallback or product pass/fail target must change.
Stop and route to /feature-to-tasks FT-002 if execution exposes a required identity, tier, dependency, acceptance, or material-scope change; do not hide it behind repair.
Stop if a provider or verification path requires a live key, unredacted artifact, live external request or evidence outside the accepted disposable/isolation route.

constraints: Weather Context owns refresh, normalization, cache/history writes, freshness, pressure trends and fallback; consumers never write its private storage.
Main Display renders the display-ready projection through Main Display → Weather Context and never reads raw provider data or private Weather Context storage.
Settings & Location owns selected location and credential validation; a city refresh is requested only after valid Settings state is persisted.
The Yandex adapter owns transport/mapping only; it does not own normalized cache/history or product fallback state.

Android OS owns device time, lifecycle and network availability. The Application Composition Root and Android Runtime Adapter provide only the accepted signal/wiring lift through existing contracts; Weather Context owns refresh cadence, cache/freshness and failure projection, and no new direct graph edge is introduced.
Selected-city API timezone drives weather dates, day boundaries and day/night selection; device timezone remains the FT-001 clock/date source.
Network/provider failure leaves the clock, timer lifecycle, cancellation and overdue dismissal usable.
All provider and test credentials are synthetic/redacted and all accepted visual effects remain static pseudo-glass.
